newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends up despite profit taking.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends up despite profit taking.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures ended higher but off their earlier highs after succumbing to late profit taking, traders said.
U.S. wheat markets climbed higher early amid continued short covering. Wheat also made gains as technical buy stops were hit, traders said.
The market's active early pace gave way to sluggish midsession dealings, and prices fell back late.
MGE spring wheat settled one to six cents per bushel higher, with Dec up six cents at $4.26-1/2. Earlier, Dec set an intraday high at $4.34 -- up 13-1/2 cents on the day.

MGE March spring wheat closed up 2-3/4 cents at $3.92-1/2. Traders said short covering helped widen the Dec/March inverted spread. It traded as far out as 35 cents Monday, after trading late Friday at 29 cents.
Traders said Cargill was a key short coverer, bull-spreading one million Dec/March bushels at 30 to 33 cents per bushel. Wilson Trading bear-spread two million March/Dec at 31 to 35 cents.
Traders said the market drew early support from news that the United States and Turkey were close to resolving some issues that had kept Turkey from importing U.S. wheat.
